chunks: From him, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about wiping over the head, and he said: “It is as though I am looking at a fold at the back of my father’s head, and he passes his hand over it.” And I asked him about wudu (ablution): should the head be wiped at its front and its back? He said: “It is as though I am looking at a fold on my father’s neck, and he wipes over it.” Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: The correct way of understanding this report is the same as what we mentioned regarding the first report, equally.
As for the report narrated by Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about wiping over the feet, how it is done. So he placed his palm upon the toes and wiped them up to the ankles, to the upper part of the foot. Then I said: May I be your ransom, what if a man were to say: with two fingers of his fingers? He said: “No, except with his palm.” Its meaning is that he would not be complete in the qualities of excellence.

key_terms.الرَّأْسِ: the head, the place wiped in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.الْفَضْلِ: excellence or added merit beyond bare validity
key_terms.الْقَدَمَيْنِ: the two feet, which are wiped in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.الْكَعْبَيْنِ: the ankles, the endpoint mentioned for wiping the feet
key_terms.الْمَسْحِ: wiping as an act in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing and wiping before salat (prayer)
key_terms.كَفَّهُ: his palm, the hand used in performing the wiping

ai.seo_question: How is wiping the head and feet performed in wudu according to the Imams عليهم السلام?
ai.summary: This report discusses the manner of masḥ in wudu (ablution), specifically wiping the head and the feet. It also preserves explanatory remarks indicating that some expressions are understood in light of other reports, and that wiping with the palm represents a more complete form of merit.
